text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: reserved-pool aurora-fin-resv at 100% GPU utilization, queue growth observed > 1m backlog, autoscaler error rate elevated. Pager triggered.
Liz H: ack. I'm oncall. what's the customer impact? which tenants on this pool?
Tom W: aurora-fin-resv is a dedicated pool for AuroraFin (enterprise). Also hosts a resv 'hyperpush' for internal perf testing — looks noisy.
Nora S: seeing queue length spike on metrics: `queue_depth: 128 -> 920` over last 6m, p95 latency climbing. CPU on head node fine, GPU util pegged.
Julian: autoscaler logs show repeated 429 from cloud provider scaling API. autoscaler retry loop backed off. looks like we've hit provider rate limits.
Liz H: summary: reserved GPUs fully used, autoscaler can't add capacity due to 429, queue keeps building, customer requests failing (AuroraFin traffic).
Marie (CS): I'm joining. AuroraFin on-call is awake, they're reporting user-facing timeouts in inference. They want ETA and mitigation.
Liz H: immediate mitigation plan: 1) identify and isolate noisy sessions 2) evict non-critical reservations (perf tests) 3) route new requests to fallback pool/shared nodes 4) attempt manual capacity bump if provider allows.
Tom W: listing tenants and sessions: `rictl reservations list --pool aurora-fin-resv --format=table` -> shows tenant hyperpush (50 sessions), aurorafin-prod (120 sessions)
Nora S: logs show hyperpush started a heavy sweep at 06:42 UTC, lots of long-running sessions. suspect runaway test harness. can we evict hyperpush?
Liz H: go for it. Evict non-critical. Tom, run safe-evict on hyperpush. add `--grace=30s`.
Tom W: running: ```
rictl reservations evict --pool aurora-fin-resv --tenant hyperpush --grace=30s --reason "noisy tenant eviction - incident 4923456790"
``` 
Tom W: eviction in progress, evicted ~48 sessions so far.
oncall-bot: INFO: eviction job accepted (job id ej-3221). Monitoring GPU reclaim.
Nora S: queue depth dropped from 920 -> 420 within 45s. p95 latency improving but still elevated.
Julian: trying manual scale: `rictl pools update --pool aurora-fin-resv --desired-replicas 18` -> provider API returned 429. retrying with exponential backoff.
Liz H: while autoscaler blocked, route new ephemeral requests to the shared-burst pool. Tom, patch routing rule to prefer shared-burst for non-SLA traffic.
Tom W: quick patch applied to routing: `routing.update prefer_shared_for pool=aurora-fin-resv if tenant != aurorafin-prod` — non-prod tenants will go to shared-burst.
Marie (CS): telling AuroraFin: we're actively evicting noisy sessions and routing non-prod off your pool. will confirm once stable.
oncall-bot: DEPLOYBOT: routing change applied by Tom W (deploy-4579).
Nora S: after eviction and routing change, GPU utilization 100% -> 82% on pool, queue depth down to 110. good recovery signal.
Liz H: still want to protect against autoscaler flapping. set autoscaler max to current+2 if provider accepts, else set a temporary reservation throttle.
Julian: provider still 429. I'm opening a support ticket with provider (SR-9342) for rate limit increase. Meanwhile, enable local throttle: `rictl pools throttle --pool aurora-fin-resv --new-arrival-rate 200r/s`.
Tom W: throttle applied. It's gracefully rejecting new reservation requests with 503 and retry-after header for non-SLA calls.
Marie (CS): AuroraFin appreciates the mitigation. Asking for timeline — we'll notify them 15m and run a phone bridge if needed.
Liz H: setting up incident bridge now. @Marie can you start the bridge and include AuroraFin primary contacts? I'll put a short status into incident channel.
Marie (CS): bridge started: https://meet.company/bridge/4923456790 - AuroraFin + CS + SRE + Eng-Platform on call.
oncall-bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INC-2026, severity P1, linked to pager 4923456790.
Liz H: next steps: - monitor queue and latency - keep hyperpush evicted - keep throttle until autoscaler healthy - escalate provider support if manual scale fails - follow up with runbook and postmortem.
Julian: provider support replied: temporary burst increase approved but needs manual operator action. I'm prepping the manual allocation plan.
Tom W: manual allocation succeeded: `rictl pools allocate --pool aurora-fin-resv --add-gpus 4 --provider-confirm` -> nodes provisioning started.
Nora S: new nodes joined, GPU util across pool normalized to 65%, queue drained to <20, p95 back to normal. AuroraFin traffic healthy.
Marie (CS): AuroraFin confirms error rate dropped to baseline and user impact mitigated. they want summary and RCA next day.
Liz H: good job. I'll convert this thread into an incident timeline and create a follow-up ticket for root cause: noisy tenant isolation + provider rate limits blocking autoscaler + lack of hard cap fallback.
Tom W: notes for RCA: add recommendation to: 1) automatic preemptive routing when queue exceeds X 2) autoscaler API backoff strategy with provider-side coordinator 3) prevent perf-test tenants on prod-reserved pools.
Marie (CS): I'll schedule a customer follow-up call with AuroraFin for tomorrow at 16:00 UTC.
oncall-bot: RESOLVE: incident 4923456790 marked resolved at 4923457090. Postmortem required within 72h.
Liz H: closing on-call items. thanks everyone. we'll run a blameless RCA and post action items.
